time_budget.transit_mode: MRT East-West Line from Changi Airport station, changing at Tanah Merah, to City Hall or Raffles Place. A Grab or taxi (about 25-30 min, SGD 20-30) is a good time-saving alternative.
time_budget.transit_cost_estimate: SGD 2-2.50 each way by MRT using a contactless card
time_budget.deadline_math: 19:00 at gate - 30 security - 50 transit back - 30 safety margin = 17:10
assumptions: Early-morning arrival bank at Changi is busy, but US passport holders can use the automated immigration lanes once the SG Arrival Card is submitted.
Bags are checked through and the traveler holds the onward boarding pass, so there is no baggage claim or check-in on return.
The return trip likely falls in the 5-6 pm rush hour, so extra time is allowed for crowded trains or expressway traffic.
At Changi, security screening happens at the gate, so the boarding buffer covers gate screening and the walk to the gate.

entry_requirements.summary: US passport holders can enter Singapore visa-free for short visits, but must submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival. Rules can change, so confirm on the official ICA Singapore website before you fly.

verdict_reason: You have over 8 hours in Singapore after every buffer, and the MRT links the airport and city reliably. Just submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before you land.

itinerary.title: MRT into the city
itinerary.location: Changi Airport MRT to Raffles Place
itinerary.description: Ride the East-West Line shuttle from Changi Airport to Tanah Merah, cross the platform toward Tuas Link, and get off at Raffles Place.
itinerary.tip: Tap in and out with a contactless Visa or Mastercard. No ticket is needed.

itinerary.title: Walk to Far East Square
itinerary.description: An easy 7-minute walk through the CBD to the original Ya Kun outlet.
itinerary.tip: Use exit H at Raffles Place and follow the signs toward Telok Ayer.

itinerary.title: Kaya toast breakfast at Ya Kun
itinerary.location: Ya Kun Kaya Toast, Far East Square
itinerary.description: Have Singapore's classic breakfast: crisp kaya toast with butter, soft-boiled eggs with soy sauce and white pepper, and a strong kopi.
itinerary.tip: Order the 'Set A'. Crack the eggs into the saucer and dip your toast.

itinerary.title: Downtown Line to the Botanic Gardens
itinerary.location: Telok Ayer MRT to Botanic Gardens MRT
itinerary.description: Ride the blue Downtown Line direct, with no changes, for about 20 minutes.
itinerary.tip: Telok Ayer station is a 3-minute walk from Ya Kun.

itinerary.title: Singapore Botanic Gardens and National Orchid Garden
itinerary.location: Singapore Botanic Gardens, Bukit Timah entrance
itinerary.description: Walk through Singapore's UNESCO-listed garden, with rainforest trails, swan lakes, and the world's largest orchid display.
itinerary.tip: Entry to the gardens is free. Only the Orchid Garden charges. Go in the morning before the heat and afternoon showers.

itinerary.title: Walk to Adam Road
itinerary.location: Botanic Gardens to Adam Road Food Centre
itinerary.description: A short walk from the gardens' Bukit Timah gate to the hawker centre.
itinerary.tip: Use the overhead bridge to cross the road.

itinerary.title: Hawker lunch at Adam Road Food Centre
itinerary.description: Try famous nasi lemak from Selera Rasa, plus mee rebus or prawn noodles, with fresh sugarcane juice.
itinerary.tip: Locals 'chope' tables with tissue packets, so don't sit where you see one. Some stalls are cash-only.

itinerary.title: Downtown Line to Gardens by the Bay
itinerary.location: Botanic Gardens MRT to Bayfront MRT
itinerary.description: Ride the Downtown Line direct to Bayfront in about 25 minutes, then follow the signs to Gardens by the Bay.
itinerary.tip: Take exit B at Bayfront and walk through the underpass.

itinerary.title: Gardens by the Bay: Cloud Forest, Flower Dome and Supertrees
itinerary.location: Gardens by the Bay, Marina Bay
itinerary.description: See Singapore's most iconic sight: a misty indoor mountain with a 35m waterfall, a giant flower conservatory, and the towering Supertree Grove.
itinerary.tip: The cool conservatories are perfect for the hot, rainy afternoon. Book online to skip the ticket queue.

itinerary.title: Walk to Marina Bay Sands
itinerary.location: Gardens by the Bay to The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands
itinerary.description: Cross the Lions Bridge to the Marina Bay Sands mall, which sits right above Bayfront MRT.
itinerary.tip: If it is pouring, use the covered underpass instead.

itinerary.title: Snack at Rasapura Masters
itinerary.location: Rasapura Masters food court, B2, Marina Bay Sands
itinerary.description: End with one last local treat: chendol, char kway teow, or a plate of carrot cake.
itinerary.tip: Bayfront MRT is right beside the food court, so stop eating by 17:05.

itinerary.title: MRT back to Changi
itinerary.location: Bayfront MRT to Changi Airport MRT
itinerary.description: Take the Downtown Line direct to Expo, then change to the East-West Line branch for Changi Airport.
itinerary.tip: This is your hard deadline. Be on the platform by 17:10, rush hour or not.

running_late_plan: If you leave the Botanic Gardens after 12:30, skip Adam Road and eat at Rasapura Masters instead.
If you are not inside Gardens by the Bay by 14:15, see only the Cloud Forest and skip the Flower Dome.
If the MRT is disrupted, take a Grab or taxi from Marina Bay Sands (about 25 min, SGD 20-30).
Leave the city by 17:10 no matter what. Skip the final snack if needed.
practical_tips: Submit the free SG Arrival Card on the official ICA site or app within 3 days before arrival, so you can use the automated immigration lanes.
Contactless cards work on the MRT and almost everywhere else. Carry about SGD 20 in cash for hawker stalls.
Changi Wi-Fi is free. Get a tourist eSIM if you want maps and Grab in the city.
November is monsoon season, so expect a short, heavy afternoon downpour. Pack a compact umbrella and keep drinking water.
At Changi, security screening happens at the gate, so arrive at the gate on time. Shops near the gate are outside screening.
Your bags are checked through, so you have nothing to collect and can head straight to departure immigration.
airport_fallback: Airside, visit the Butterfly Garden in Terminal 3, the Sunflower Garden in Terminal 2, and the free movie theatre.
The Ambassador Transit Lounge and the airside Aerotel offer showers and day-use rooms for a nap.
Since you can enter visa-free, you could also clear immigration just to see the HSBC Rain Vortex and the Canopy Park at Jewel, connected to Terminal 1.
